artboards.title: C — One canvas, all the way down

annotations.text:
Pick a direction — these are four different answers to ONE question: how do you navigate a system with this many dimensions (physical / L2 / L3 / power, campus → building → closet → rack → device → port, ownership, IP, link type)?

The six-tab bar from the first pass is wrong and none of these use it.

They are deliberately rough. Judge the navigation idea, not the pixels.

True in ALL FOUR, so not a differentiator:

• Racks group, one by default, size is editable
• Equipment carries its real port complement from the engine — count, position, and type (copper / fibre / power)
• Drag a port to a port to cable it
• A cable can end in a PORTAL — up or down — meaning it leaves this view. Not an unknown, just elsewhere
• Owner is a property of equipment, filterable everywhere
• Physical / L2 / L3 are the same graph, drawn differently — never separate drawings that drift apart
The first pass, kept only for density and token reference. Its six-tab navigation is superseded by whichever direction you pick on page 1.
